title: Cost Craftsman: workload profiling, heuristic lattice, and safe continuous batching parameters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a generalizable recommendation engine that profiles live inference workloads, derives a compact workload signature (heuristic lattice), and produces safe, incremental batching + caching parameter updates. Goal: reduce per-token cost while keeping latency and quality within SLOs. This ticket covers: workload fingerprint schema, risk-scoring heuristics, shadow-simulation harness, and a staged apply/rollback controller for continuous parameter updates.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler produces deterministic workload signatures for 95% of observed routes over a 24h window
Recommendation engine outputs parameter candidates (min_batch, max_batch, coalesce_window_ms, kv_cache_policy) with an estimated cost delta and risk score
Shadow-simulations on historical traces predict cost delta within 10% of actual after apply in 3/4 test datasets
Safe-apply controller supports graduated rollout (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with automatic rollback triggers and audit logging
Runbook created with rollback thresholds and manual override steps reviewed by SRE and PM
technical_design: High-level approach: 1) Profiling: collect per-route time-series for request size distribution, prefix-repeat entropy, KV cache hit/miss, sequence lengths, arrival process (inter-arrival CDF), and observed microburst patterns. Store compact signatures computed as hashed histograms + lightweight sketches (bucketed token-length, 5-95 percentile of prefix similarity, and short-term burstiness index). 2) Heuristic lattice: define orthogonal heuristic axes (cost-sensitivity, latency-sensitivity, cache-friendliness, burst-tolerance). Each workload signature maps to a point in this 4D lattice; rules traverse lattice to propose parameter families instead of single values. 3) Recommendation scoring: combine expected per-token cost reduction (from simulated coalescing) with risk_penalty = alpha*latency_risk + beta*error_risk + gamma*quality_risk. 4) Simulation harness: replay sampled traces against runtime model of KV cache and batching to predict cost/latency/kv-hit changes. 5) Safe-apply controller: incremental traffic ramp with shadow comparisons, canary cohorts by customer tiers, and enforced cool-down windows. Metrics computed at each step update rollout decision. Implementation notes: profiler runs as a service reading ingestion stream (1s granularity), signatures stored in time-partitioned table, simulator is deterministic and unit-tested with golden traces.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal lab experiments using offline traces (owners: Marcus Chen, Priya Rao). Phase 1: shadow-sim on 5 low-risk routes; validate estimator accuracy. Phase 2: 1% live traffic canary for 24h; monitor metrics and auto-promote to 10% if thresholds hold. Phase 3: staged roll to 50% and 100% over multiple business hours. Rollback triggers: p95 latency increased > 15% absolute or relative error rate increase > 0.4% or model-quality eval drop > 2.0% on sampled prompts. Emergency manual rollback path in console with audit record.
monitoring_queries_and_dashboards: Example query: SELECT route, percentile(request_tokens,95) as p95_tokens, avg(kv_hit) as kv FROM inference_signals WHERE ts >= now() - interval '24h' GROUP BY route
